# Can Claude Build a Mobile App and Publish It to the App Store? (2026)


Claude can write the code for a mobile app, but it cannot publish it to the App Store for you. If people will open your app from a link, a home screen icon is enough. If they need to find it in App Store search, you need your own developer account, a real build, and Apple's review.


## The short version


Claude writes mobile app code. It does not own a store account or press submit.


Publishing costs $99 a year with Apple and $25 once with Google Play.


There are three kinds of mobile app, and only two of them go through store review.


On Floot, the phone version shares the backend your web app already runs on.


On other tools, the code arrives first and the server, database, and build are left to you.


The rest of this guide covers the three kinds of mobile app, what publishing requires, which kind you need, and what each tool makes you do.


## Building and publishing, in one picture


Think of a book. Claude can write the manuscript. A bookstore will not shelve it just because it exists.


The store only takes books from a publisher it has a contract with, and it reads each one first. On the App Store, the publisher is your developer account, and the reader is Apple's review team.


The split exists because Apple ties every app to a person who pays and answers for it.


## The three kinds of mobile app


A "mobile app" can mean three things, and only two go through review.


Home screen app. What it is: A web app saved to the phone with its own icon. Store review: No.


Wrapped web app. What it is: Your website inside an app shell. Store review: Yes, and high rejection risk if it is only the website.


Native app. What it is: Code built for the phone (React Native, Expo, Swift). Store review: Yes, normal review.


A home screen app is free and live the same day. A native app is the only kind in App Store search.


## What publishing actually requires


Publishing takes four things, and none of them is code.


It **needs an account** . Apple charges $99 a year and Google Play $25 once (as of Sept 25, 2026). If the Apple membership lapses, your apps come off the store.


It **needs a real build** . That usually means Xcode on a Mac, or a cloud service like Expo EAS.


It **needs consent before data goes to an AI** . Since November 13, 2025, Apple's guideline 5.1.2(i) requires apps to "clearly disclose where personal data will be shared with third parties, including with third-party AI, and obtain explicit permission before doing so." (An app that sends notes to Claude for a summary needs a consent screen first.)


It **needs a review** , by a person at Apple or Google.


Notice the pattern. Every one of those belongs to the account owner, which is you.


## Which kind do you need?


Here is the quick test. Ask how people will find your app.


If they will find it through a link you send, you can skip the store. A client portal, a booking page, and an internal tool all work as a home screen app.


If they will search the App Store, you need a native build. So does anything needing the camera or push notifications.


## What each tool makes you do


Every tool gets you mobile code. The difference is what lands on you.


Claude in chat writes a project folder. You install the build tools and set up the server and database yourself.


Claude Code can run build and submit commands, with your account. Expo EAS removes the Mac and adds no backend.


The pattern is the same everywhere it goes wrong: the screens look done, then the first login sends you off to set up a server.


Floot builds the mobile app for you as part of the same project, so the phone version and the web version share one backend. You ask for "a phone version," and Floot gives you an instant Add to Home Screen app plus downloadable Xcode and Android projects for store submission. The logins, data, and endpoints behind it are the ones already running on your live URL. Mobile builds are metered: Free 2 a month, Pro 12, Power unlimited.


Because Floot also includes the database, logins with Google, Microsoft, and email, file storage, email sending, scheduled jobs, and live updates, the backend a mobile app normally needs its own server for is already there. You never sign up for anything else. What stays yours is the store itself: your developer account, Apple's and Google's fees, and their review.


## FAQ


## Can Claude submit my app to the App Store?


No. Only the developer account owner can submit, even when Claude Code runs the command.


## Will Apple reject my app because AI wrote it?


No. Apple reviews what the app does. Thin website wrappers and missing AI data consent are the common problems.


## How much does it cost to put an app on the App Store?


$99 a year for Apple and $25 once for Google Play, as of Sept 25, 2026.


## Do I need a Mac to publish an iPhone app?


No. Cloud build services like Expo EAS build iOS apps without one.


## Did Apple ban apps made with vibe coding?


No. The March 2026 block hit app-builder apps like Replit and Vibecode, not the apps people build with them.


## Does Floot build mobile apps?


Yes. Floot makes an Add to Home Screen version plus Xcode and Android projects on your web app's backend.
